'''Regina Nuzzo''' is a professor of statistics at [[Gallaudet University]] in [[Washington, D.C.|Washington D.C.]], a liberal arts school for deaf and hard-of-hearing students. She also writes articles about the importance of statistical and science communication and is an advocate for people with disabilities in the science and technology field.<ref>{{Cite web |title=WoW Seminar April 21, 6:30-8:00pm |url=https://deafscientists.com/2016/04/wow-seminar-april-21-630-800pm/ |access-date=2025-11-08 |website=Rochester Bridges to the Doctorate |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Education ==
Nuzzo graduated from the [[University of South Florida]] with a [[bachelor's degree]] in [[industrial engineering]] and went on to obtain her [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D]] in statistics from [[Stanford University]] in 2004, supervised by [[Richard A. Olshen]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Regina Nuzzo |url=https://statistics.stanford.edu/people/regina-nuzzo |access-date=2020-03-25 |website=Stanford University Department of Statistics}}</ref> Her dissertation was written on the usage of [[Stochastic process|stochastic models]] in [[biochemistry]].

Nuzzo also graduated from the [[University of California, Santa Cruz|University of California Santa Cruz's]] science writing program.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CV |url=https://www.reginanuzzo.com/files/cv.pdf |access-date=2025-11-08 |website=Regina Nuzzo}}</ref>

== Career ==
Nuzzo has been a faculty member at Gallaudet University since 2006. She has written multiple articles for publication in major magazines, including [[Wired (magazine)|''WIRED'']] magazine, the [[The New York Times|''New York Times'']], [[Los Angeles Times|''Los Angeles Times'']], as well as [[Reader's Digest|''Reader's Digest'']]. In addition to teaching, she gives seminars about statistics, which have been hosted at the [[University of Washington]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.biostat.washington.edu/node/9907|title=Biostatistics Seminar: Regina Nuzzo {{!}} Department of Biostatistics|website=www.biostat.washington.edu|access-date=2020-03-25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Biostatistics Seminar: Regina Nuzzo |url=https://www.biostat.washington.edu/node/9907 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200325181552/https://www.biostat.washington.edu/node/9907 |archive-date=2020-03-25 |access-date=2025-11-08 |website=University of Washington Department of Biostatistics |language=en}}</ref> the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Grand Rounds with Regina Nuzzo |url=https://sph.umd.edu/multimedia/grand-rounds-regina-nuzzo |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200325181549/https://sph.umd.edu/multimedia/grand-rounds-regina-nuzzo |archive-date=2020-03-25 |access-date= |website=UMD School of Public Health |language=en}}</ref> and [[Harvard University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Regina Nuzzo |url=https://www.hsph.harvard.edu/biostatistics/tag/regina-nuzzo/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210410184619/https://www.hsph.harvard.edu/biostatistics/tag/regina-nuzzo/ |archive-date=2021-04-10 |access-date= |website=Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health Department of Biostatistics |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2019, Nuzzo was appointed the Senior Advisor for Statistics Communication and Media Innovation for the [[American Statistical Association]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=ASA Welcomes Regina Nuzzo as Senior Advisor for Statistics Communication and Media Innovation |url=https://www.amstat.org/news-listing/2021/10/08/asa-welcomes-regina-nuzzo-as-senior-advisor-for-statistics-communication-and-media-innovation |access-date=2025-11-08 |website=American Statistical Association}}</ref>

== Awards ==
In 2014, Nuzzo was awarded the Excellence in Statistical Reporting Award (ESRA) by the American Statistical Association for her article in [[Nature (journal)|''Nature'']] about statistical [[p-value]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Nuzzo|first=Regina|date=2014-02-13|title=Scientific method: Statistical errors|journal=Nature News|language=en|volume=506|issue=7487|pages=150–152|doi=10.1038/506150a|pmid=24522584|bibcode=2014Natur.506..150N|doi-access=free|hdl=11573/685222|hdl-access=free}}</ref>
